description: createToken also creates JWTs (https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/token-api, "Creating a new JWT Token"): "If we provide an `expiration_time` in the URL, the token will be created as a JWT Token", and the example sends the scopes as a JSON body: `POST /v0/tokens?name=jwt_token&expiration_time=1710000000 -d '{"scopes": [{"type": "PIPES:READ", "resource": "requests_per_day", "fixed_params": {"user_id": 3}}]}'`. The request parameters table lists neither, so `expiration_time` is added as a query parameter (Unix seconds) and `scopes` as a JSON body member whose `fixed_params` are caller-named template parameters pinned into the token. The JWT response adds `exp` and per-scope `fixed_params` to the token shape. Live (2026-11-18): POST /v0/tokens?name=...&expiration_time=<now+300> with that body answered 200 `{token, name, exp, scopes: [{type, resource, fixed_params: {city: "Oslo"}}]}`; createToken passes ResponseValidation.strict; queryPipe on distilled_endpoint (default city Chicago) with the returned JWT answered only the Oslo row, and the same JWT on another pipe answered 403 (Forbidden).

traits.smithy.api#documentation: Optional. Expiry as a Unix timestamp in seconds. When set, the token is created as a JWT with the `scopes` of the body.
JWT scopes, sent as the JSON body. Only used with `expiration_time`; static tokens take `scope`.
The Pipe or Data Source the scope grants.
Template parameters pinned into the token: every query made with it uses these values, whatever the caller sends.
JWT expiry as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Only on JWTs.
Template parameters pinned into a JWT scope.
